# Results — Study 817 (Realized-Volatility Trend)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: sort a
cross-section on the **trend** in realized vol — each name's `(trailing 21d realized vol) /
(trailing 63d realized vol) - 1` — long the **falling-vol** names, short the **rising-vol**
names, betting rising vol keeps de-rating and falling vol re-rates. Offline & deterministic
once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30**
(the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint
`5384b8f7f128` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **vol trend** = `(trailing 21d realized vol) / (trailing 63d realized vol) - 1` (realized vol = std of daily simple returns), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the bottom 30%** (most falling vol), **short the top 30%** (most rising vol), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled falling-vs-rising books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a **level-vs-trend additivity regression** against the low-vol level anomaly; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. Delisted
and de-rated names — exactly the ones whose vol trend would have run hardest before they left
the index — are absent.

## The headline — long-falling-vol / short-rising-vol spread

Daily equal-weight bottom-30% minus top-30% vol-trend spread (n = **4,083** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long falling-vol − short rising-vol)** | **+0.94 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+0.86** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.83 |
| falling-vol book / rising-vol book | +7.74 bps / +6.80 bps (Welch *t* = +0.36) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | +0.21 |

The spread has the **claimed sign** (falling-vol names very slightly out-earn rising-vol
names) but is **statistically indistinguishable from zero** — NW *t* = **+0.86**, well below
the |t| ≥ 2 bar. The vol *trend* carries essentially no cross-sectional return information on
50 liquid US mega-caps.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) tilt a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the vol-trend sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted** panel
(signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+0.94 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.021 bps (0.883) |
| position of observed | ≈ **+1.09σ** above the placebo mean (right-tail p = **0.121**) |

The observed spread sits barely one sigma into the right tail — comfortably inside what the
permutation null produces by chance. Not distinguishable from noise.

## Additivity — is the vol TREND anything beyond the low-vol LEVEL (330)?

The whole point of the study is to separate vol *momentum* from the low-vol *level* anomaly.
We build the plain low-vol level sort (long low 63d-vol, short high 63d-vol) on the same tape,
then regress the trend spread on the level spread and read the residual (Newey-West) *t*:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| low-vol **level** spread (330-style) | **−4.74 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−2.61**) |
| corr(trend spread, level spread) | +0.065 |
| trend spread β on level spread | +0.038 |
| **trend alpha net of level** | **+1.12 bps/day** (NW *t* = **+1.02**) |

Two honest readings. First, the low-vol *level* anomaly itself **inverts** on this mega-cap
survivor tape (−4.74 bps/day, NW *t* = −2.61: high-vol mega-caps *out-earned* low-vol ones over
2010–2026, the familiar tech-momentum sign-flip). Second, the trend and level spreads are
nearly **uncorrelated** (corr +0.065), so the vol trend is indeed a *distinct* axis — but its
alpha net of the level effect is only **+1.12 bps/day (NW *t* = +1.02)**, not significant. The
trend is orthogonal to the level, and **equally empty**: nothing additive survives.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,949) | +1.52 bps | +1.15 |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | +0.41 bps | +0.24 |

Weakly positive in both halves, significant in neither — no era rescues the signal.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +0.94 bps | 2.14 bps | **−1.20 bps** | −1.06 | −0.26 | −3.0%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +0.94 bps | 10.14 bps | **−9.20 bps** | −8.14 | −2.02 | −23.2%/yr |

The +0.94 bps/day gross edge is smaller than the **2.14 bps/day** round-trip friction at a
mere 1 bp one-way, so the book is already **net negative** at the lowest realistic cost and
bleeds badly at 5 bps. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel with a persistent latent "vol-trend tilt" that modulates each
name's return-vol amplitude and (with `edge>0`) depresses its forward mean when vol is rising.
No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.18** (sd 1.03), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.0015`, seed 817) | **+9.49** (Welch *t* = +9.29) |

The detector recovers a *planted* rising-vol-derates relation cleanly and never fires on the
null — so the flat real-tape result is a genuine absence of edge, not a broken sort.
*(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The vol *trend* — distinct from the low-vol level anomaly by
  construction (corr with the level spread is +0.065) — carries **no** reliable
  cross-sectional return signal on 50 liquid US mega-caps. The long-falling-vol /
  short-rising-vol spread is **+0.94 bps/day** (NW *t* = **+0.86**): the *claimed* sign, but
  statistically zero, sitting only +1.09σ into a 1,000-permutation placebo, weak in both eras
  (*t* = +1.15 / +0.24), and adding just +1.12 bps/day (*t* = +1.02) on top of the (itself
  inverted) level effect. The clean 20-seed synthetic control confirms the machinery works, so
  the flat result is real. The trend is **not additive** — it is orthogonal to the level and
  equally empty.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The +0.94 bps/day gross edge is smaller than the 2.14 bps/day
  round-trip friction at 1 bp one-way; the book is net **−1.20 bps/day** at 1 bp and
  **−9.20 bps/day** at 5 bps. Nothing to trade.
